items.textToSpeech: For adults aged 18+, including those pregnant or lactating, the Tolerable Upper Intake Level for vitamin E is 300 milligrams per day. Oral intakes of high amounts of vitamin E can increase blood coagulation defects in subjects with vitamin K deficiency caused by malabsorption or due to therapy with anticoagulants. Therefore the Upper Level does not apply to patients receiving anticoagulant drugs, to patients with malabsorption syndromes, or to other conditions where the synthesis of vitamin K by the gut microflora might be impaired. The Tolerable Upper Intake Level is the maximum level of total chronic intake of a nutrient from all sources judged to be unlikely to pose a risk of adverse health effects in humans. For the European Union, Dietary Reference Values are published by the European Food Safety Authority Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies. Is there anything else I can help you with?
